learningObjectives: Explain application versioning in a scenario.

elements.description: Version format is major-minor-patch. Lock and roll creates an empty higher version for incremental edits; untouched Rules remain resolved from accessible earlier versions. Skimming consolidates latest eligible Rules from a selected major into a higher minor or major. Available, Final and Blocked are copied; Not Available is excluded; Withdrawn survives minor skims only. Check in work before versioning. New major/minor releases require application and Access Group updates; patch changes typically do not.

elements.text: Worked example: Pricing:02-03-01 holds Rules A and B; 02-03-02 updates B. A minor skim consolidates A with the newer B. Lock and roll instead starts an empty editable version.

examPitfalls.title: Empty vs consolidated
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Lock and roll copies all existing Rules.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Distinguish empty version creation from skim consolidation.

examPitfalls.title: Skim scope
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A skim merges every major version.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Identify the selected major before predicting results.

examPitfalls.title: Status nuance
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Minor includes it; major excludes it.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A small fix changes only one Rule. Which method creates an empty version for that edit?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Incremental work uses an empty new version; a skim consolidates existing Rules.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Application versioning. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Skimming consolidates existing rules; this edit needs an empty version.
optionExplanations.B: An empty patch isolates the changed rule.
optionExplanations.C: Product Preview inspects packaging, not version creation.
optionExplanations.D: Circumstancing specializes a rule, not a release.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Rate exists in 01-01-01, but only Letter changes in 01-01-02. Both patches are accessible. Where can unchanged Rate resolve?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Creating a patch does not require copying every unchanged Rule.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Application versioning. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Accessible older patches can supply unchanged rules.
optionExplanations.B: Crossing a major version is unnecessary here.
optionExplanations.C: Rate remains eligible in the accessible older patch.
optionExplanations.D: The accessible Rate instance still exists.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Ruleset has A and B in 02-01-01, and newer B in 02-01-03. What does a minor skim consolidate?
practiceQuiz.rationale: A skim carries the latest eligible instance of each Rule.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Application versioning. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: A remains and the newer B replaces its predecessor.
optionExplanations.B: This would discard the eligible B update.
optionExplanations.C: Two default copies would defeat consolidation.
optionExplanations.D: An empty version describes rolling, not skimming.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO availability statuses are copied during both major and minor skims?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Final and Blocked survive both; Withdrawn differs by skim type.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Application versioning. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Neither skim retains Not Available rules.
optionExplanations.B: Final is retained by both skim types.
optionExplanations.C: Both retain Blocked to preserve blocking effects.
optionExplanations.D: Only the minor skim retains Withdrawn.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which status is carried by a minor skim but excluded by a major skim?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Minor and major skims handle Withdrawn differently.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Application versioning. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.D: Withdrawn survives minor, not major, skimming.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A skim selects major 03. Must Rules that exist only in major 02 be copied?

options.text: No, the selected major defines scope
Only if the operator logs in again

practiceQuiz.rationale: Skimming does not merge every historical major.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Application versioning. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Skimming is scoped, not a historical merge.
optionExplanations.B: Major 02 is outside the selected source scope.
optionExplanations.C: Unlocking does not expand source scope.
optionExplanations.D: Login does not change which versions are skimmed.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO actions belong before a release versioning operation?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Know the version stack and make intended edits available to the operation.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Application versioning. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Check-in makes intended shared edits eligible.
optionExplanations.B: Deleting history is not a versioning prerequisite.
optionExplanations.C: Stack knowledge prevents choosing the wrong release scope.
optionExplanations.D: Specialization is unrelated to preparing a release.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A release moves to a new major version. Which references need review?

options.text: Application and Access Group version references

practiceQuiz.rationale: A major release must be reachable through the application configuration.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Application versioning. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Theme styling cannot redirect application versions.
optionExplanations.B: Urgency affects work priority, not release selection.
optionExplanations.C: Both references must point to the intended release.
optionExplanations.D: Quiz labels cannot configure runtime access.

quickRecap.value: Empty new version for incremental edits; eligible older Rules still resolve.
Consolidate latest eligible Rules from the selected major.
Both: Available, Final, Blocked. Neither: Not Available. Minor only: Withdrawn.
Review application and Access Group references for major/minor changes.
